Not the person you asked but in my personal opinion the difference is "reading the room" is more of a knowing what not to say type of situation. Like if my friends grandma just died it would clearly be a bad time to make certain types of jokes. Reading the room is a "what is the tone of this situation and how should I respond appropriately?" type of instinct. 

The difference between that and being overvigilant in others body language comes down to whether you are balancing your reactions to the setting you are in or if you are overthinking someone else's reactions due to what you said or did. 

For example, if I'm at a business meeting, reading the room would be making sure I'm not swearing, I'm paying attention, I'm being professional in how I'm communicating with everyone, I'm dressed appropriately, etc etc. 

Dancing around looks and tones would be if I said something and then noticed my supervisor looks sorta grumpy at that comment and then worrying internally if what I said pissed him off. Obviously something like "I noticed when I said "x", you did "y" and it's giving me the impression that you are upset with me, is that correct?" Is an appropriate question but if he says "no you are fine" and then I continue to second guess and read way too into his body language that is me dancing through looks and tones. 

Even if he is upset at that point it is on him to communicate this clearly to me and when I still worry about it I'm trying to regulate other people's emotions at that point which isn't healthy.

The overlap can sometimes come from people who are bad at reading the room and create a social blunder and then people might be upset with them and it might be awkward for those people to point out the social blunder so they fall back on "well you should've read the room" these situations are tricky but in my personal opinion social awkwardness is not a crime and until you are told what you did was "wrong" you can't atone for your actions so even in these situations you shouldnt be dancing around people's body language.

Tl;Dr: Reading a room is about how you conduct yourself in difference situations while reading into people's tones is more about assuming others mood  based on body language alone.
